name: SFX Kit
description: 320 original sound effects for videos, animations and interfaces, with the data an AI tool needs to choose, place and mix each one.
credit: Not required. If you'd like to: "SFX Kit by Wyzowl" (https://github.com/wyzowl/sfx-kit).

how_to_use.find: GUIDE.md lists common on-screen moments with sounds made for them. A sound's use_for, avoid_for and tags say what it suits; its variant how it differs from its siblings (softer or harder, lighter or heavier, shorter or longer); fits_seconds the length of moment it fits.
how_to_use.place: Start every sound at (the moment it should meet) − sync.at. sync.at already points at the part of the sound that should meet the moment (the hit, the start of a gesture, a sequence's first event even when a later one is louder, the till's bell), so this one rule holds for every sound. sync.meets says what kind of moment that is (instant, action-start, move-peak, arrival or release) and sync.how says it in words; where it says to start a sound with an action, its sync point (where it becomes audible) meets the action's first frame. If you change a sound's rate, divide its times by the rate. If a start falls before 0, start at 0 and trim that much off the sound's beginning.
how_to_use.fit: span_seconds is the length of moment a sound fits at rate 1, so the rate that fits a moment exactly is span_seconds ÷ its length, within adapt.rate (fits_seconds is that range; a whoosh has no span, and its fits_seconds are the lengths of move it suits). A sound that runs with an action can lose its end, and a build that ends on its sync point its start; to drop a later part, cut just before its time in parts. Trims are in the file's own seconds (after a rate change, a trim of t is t ÷ rate on the timeline). The files start and end on silence, so a cut part-way through a sound needs a short fade (10 to 50 ms, or 300 ms or more for a long tail).
how_to_use.levels: Gains are relative to each file as it is (0 dB). Every file sits on one loudness scale (level.lufs is its loudest 150 ms), so the sounds are level with each other as they are, and a category's intensities differ in level on purpose. At 0 dB a medium effect's loudest moment is about −20.5 LUFS, a few dB under a voiceover mixed to about −16 LUFS integrated. under_voiceover_db is how far a sound comes down wherever its body (timing.onset to timing.body_end) overlaps speech, for the voice to stay clear over it. A sound whose avoid_for starts 'On top of speech' masks or competes with a voice even when it's lowered.
how_to_use.tuning: The tuned sounds are in C major, so they agree with each other: most only on its pentatonic notes (tuning: C major pentatonic), which also sit with music in G or F major, or in A, E or D minor. Sounds with adapt.rate [1, 1] keep their rate: the tuned ones, and a few whose pitch must stay true.

loudness.measure: level.lufs is the loudest 150 ms of the sound, K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770), in LUFS. Mono sounds are measured as if played on both speakers.
loudness.tiers: Each category sets the levels of its intensities on this one scale, so soft and hard stay apart and categories sit together. Bass-heavy sounds feel louder than they measure: the scale weighs low frequencies lightly.

sounds.name: Whoosh, fast and hard
sounds.description: A fast, crisp whip of air with a bright edge and a little push behind it.
avoid_for: Calm or corporate pieces
Small UI details
On top of speech: use a softer one

sync.how: Ease-in-out: put the sync point at the middle of the move. Ease-out (fast start, slowing to a stop): about a quarter of the way in. Ease-in (slow start, fast exit): about three quarters of the way in.

adapt.notes: To fit a move up to about 15% shorter or 20% longer, play it faster or slower (its pitch moves with it); beyond that, use the next speed. Adjust level with gain, but for a clearly softer or harder sound use the other intensity rather than a big gain change.

pairs_with.how: Something landing: the whoosh on the move (its sync point at the move's fastest point) and the impact on the frame it lands. A whoosh that suits the move's length dies away just before the landing; use one a step softer than the impact.
Something arriving and appearing: the whoosh during the move, the pop as it lands, at a lower gain than the whoosh.
A reveal: the whoosh into the reveal, the shimmer starting at the whoosh's sync point.

use_for: Something collapsing or shrinking into a point
The build into a hard cut, a hit or a reveal
An element pulled back into a button or icon
avoid_for: Moments that should land softly (it stops dead)
Big, energetic moments (use strong)

sync.how: Place it so its end (the sync point) lands on the moment of collapse, the cut or the hit: start = that moment − sync.at.

adapt.notes: For other lengths, pick the nearest one and trim its quiet start rather than changing the rate.

pairs_with.how: A pull into a hit: the reverse whoosh, its end on the impact's sync point.
A big moment: the reverse whoosh into a boom starting on its sync point.
Something sucked into a point and gone: the reverse whoosh with a small pop out at its end, at −6 dB.
